entity: Groupon UK entity (one of five listed in Exhibit 21.1 — employing entity to confirm)
summary: 5.6 weeks in two buckets with different legal rules (4 weeks EU-derived, 1.6 weeks domestic), capped at 28 days; bank holidays may count toward it; no statutory right to bank holidays off.

owner.role: Employment counsel (UK) + HR Business Partner London

locationAssumption.citation: Employees assumed to work in England (Scotland/NI have different bank holidays)

rule.citation: WTR 1998 reg.13/13A: leave measured in weeks of the worker's own pattern

source.citation: Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971 + royal proclamation; gov.uk/bank-holidays (England & Wales)

rule.citation: No statutory right to bank holidays off; Groupon assumed to count them toward the 5.6 weeks (statutory-minimum contracts)
rule.note: If contracts give bank holidays in addition, set deductFromEntitlement=false — one-field change.

rule.citation: WTR 1998 reg.15A: in the first year leave accrues at 1/12 per month; thereafter granted at the start of the leave year (Groupon policy assumption)
rule.note: Reg.15A runs for 12 months from the start date with combined rounding to half-days; the engine applies it to the calendar hire year and rounds per bucket — a known simplification.

rule.citation: WTR 1998 reg.13(9) as amended by SI 2023/1426 (from 1 Jan 2024): no carry-forward, except (14) statutory family leave, (15) sickness — up to 18 months — and (16)–(17) where the employer did not give a reasonable opportunity, encourage the worker to take the leave, or warn that it would be lost; it then carries until the end of the first full leave year in which that is cured (18)
rule.note: Modelled like Germany: lapses at the start of the next leave year only if the worker was warned; otherwise kept. The sickness and family-leave routes are not modelled.

rule.citation: No WTR provision: the right to retake leave lost to sickness rests on case law (CJEU Pereda C-277/08, ANGED C-78/11; NHS Leeds v Larner [2012] EWCA Civ 1034) and applies to the 4-week leave
rule.note: Counsel to confirm the post-2024 position.

rule.citation: WTR 1998 reg.14: payment in lieu only on termination, pro-rated (A × B) − C
rule.note: Reg.14: (A × B) − C; reg.14(6) also pays carried-over leave.

rule.citation: WTR 1998 reg.13A: additional 1.6 weeks; total capped at 28 days (reg.13A(3))
WTR 1998 reg.15A: in the first year leave accrues at 1/12 per month; thereafter granted at the start of the leave year (Groupon policy assumption)
rule.note: Reg.15A runs for 12 months from the start date with combined rounding to half-days; the engine applies it to the calendar hire year and rounds per bucket — a known simplification.

rule.citation: WTR 1998 reg.13A(7): may be carried into the next leave year by relevant agreement
rule.note: Groupon policy of up to 5 days is an assumption. Reg.13A(7A) adds carry-forward for family leave.

rule.citation: No WTR provision: the right to retake leave lost to sickness rests on case law (CJEU Pereda C-277/08, ANGED C-78/11; NHS Leeds v Larner [2012] EWCA Civ 1034) and applies to the 4-week leave
rule.note: Counsel to confirm the post-2024 position.

rule.citation: WTR 1998 reg.14: payment in lieu only on termination, pro-rated (A × B) − C
rule.note: Reg.14: (A × B) − C; reg.14(6) also pays carried-over leave.

extras.label: Irregular-hours workers
extras.citation: WTR 1998 reg.15B (SI 2023/1426): 12.07% of hours worked for leave years from 1 April 2024
extras.note: Not modelled — no irregular-hours staff in dataset.

extras.label: Holiday records
extras.citation: WTR 1998 reg.16B (inserted by Employment Rights Act 2025 s.35, in force 6 April 2026): employers must keep adequate records of holiday and holiday pay for 6 years; failing to is an offence
extras.note: The append-only ledger, with a citation on every line, is that record.

extras.label: Leave year
extras.citation: WTR 1998 reg.13(3): without a relevant agreement the leave year starts on each anniversary of the start date
extras.note: The engine assumes Groupon UK has a relevant agreement setting a calendar leave year — verify.
